newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 23.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* Philippine president Fidel Ramos in hospital undergoing a series of medical tests to determine if he needs heart surgery.
* On Friday, the Dow Jones rose 10.76 points to 6,484.40. PLDT's ADR fell $3.25 to $54.25.
* On Friday, the peso weakened to 26.301 to a U.S. dollar from 26.288.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed at 3,180.20, up 25.82.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rate was down at 10.8125 pct from 10.84375 pct.
* The proposed 1997 national budget will not be passed by Congress despite a two-day special session called by President Fidel Ramos, several newspapers report.
* The gross international reserves reach $11.8 billion as of last Friday from $11.6 in end-November, Central Bank treasury head Sergio Edeza says.
* Trading of Centennial City Inc shares resumes today at the Philippine Stock Exchange following the Securities and Exchange Commission's lifting of the suspension order last Friday.

* Newspaper Today reports that stockholders of Mondragon International Philippines Inc are expected to ratify the company's decision to give up its consumer product line and turn it to the Gonzalez family.
* Newspapers say the Central bank is planning to require a 25 percent loan loss requirement for banks which have lent to the real estate sector.
* Five foreign and local companies have tied up for the proposed 200-billion peso Mindanao railway system that will link 15 cities and towns in southern Philippines.
